She is also due for her routine nail care.", "start_char":58, "end_char":153}],"hpi":[{"text":"59-year-old female with a long-standing history of bilateral hallux valgus presents with new pain at her right first MTP medial eminence. Pain began approximately two weeks ago after she purchased new dress shoes for her daughter's wedding. The pain is localized to the bunion prominence with shoe wear and resolves when barefoot. No swelling, no redness, no fever. She denies any acute injury. Separately, she is due for routine debridement of dystrophic toenails; last service was 14 weeks ago.", "start_char":179, "end_char":550}],"exam_findings":[{"text":"Right foot first MTP: prominent medial eminence consistent with chronic hallux valgus deformity. Tender to direct palpation over the bursa. No erythema, no warmth, no fluctuance, no skin breakdown. Range of motion at the first MTP within functional limits, mild pain at end-range. No inflammatory arthritis findings. Bilateral toenails: thickened with subungual debris on multiple nails, consistent with onychomycosis. Both feet: pulses +2, no edema, no other lesions.", "start_char":563, "end_char":935}],"mdm":[{"text":"Right hallux valgus with new symptomatic medial bunion bursitis secondary to shoe pressure. This is a separate and clearly identifiable problem. Plan: counseled on shoe modification (wider toe box, soft upper materials), recommended over-the-counter bunion shield for upcoming wedding, NSAID as needed. If conservative measures fail, will discuss orthotic management or surgical consultation. Return in 6 weeks for re-evaluation. Separately, patient is due for routine podiatric nail care; meets indication and frequency requirements for Modifier 25-bearing visit.", "start_char":949, "end_char":1345}],"procedure_note":[{"text":"Following informed consent: ten dystrophic toenails debrided using sterile technique. Patient tolerated well, no complications.", "start_char":1357, "end_char":1451}],"ambiguous_segments":[]}
